question.text: Shivalik Opportunities Fund (Cat II) issues side-letters to three anchor LPs granting enhanced information rights and fee waivers. Per SEBI's pari-passu framework and PPM templates, the Manager must disclose which of the following?

answer.text: Nothing — side letters are confidential between the fund and the anchor LPs
Only the fee waiver needs disclosure; information rights are exempt
Disclosure is required only during SEBI inspection

All differential rights, eligibility criteria and method of availing them must be transparently disclosed in the PPM; differential rights not in SFA standards must be reported to SEBI (aifreporting@sebi.gov.in) in the prescribed format within the specified timeline; rights adversely affecting others must be terminated

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the pari-passu rights framework (SEBI (AIF) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations and SEBI Circular dated Dec 13, 2024): differential rights may be offered to select investors WITHOUT affecting others' interest, subject to: (i) all differential rights and eligibility criteria transparently disclosed in PPM, (ii) rights reported to SEBI if outside SFA implementation standards, (iii) any right ascertained as affecting other investors must be immediately terminated. Pari-passu requirement does not apply to AI-only Funds. **The Trap:** Option A ignores disclosure mandate (side-letters are NOT private under AIF). Option B partitions treatment wrongly. Option C is reactive (compliance is proactive). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests differential-rights. Private equity industry convention uses 'Most-Favoured-Nation' (MFN) language — SFA standards formalise these. LP-GP side-letter norms also tracked under ILPA guidelines (not Indian law but relevant comparator). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Consolidate all side-letters into an 'MFN Annexure' to PPM, listing each right with eligibility (e.g., 'commitment > INR 50 cr' for co-invest rights, 'commitment > INR 100 cr' for fee waiver). This transparency prevents SEBI challenging differentiated rights as undisclosed priority distribution.
